_comment: Stage 4. Ranked acquisition strategies. rank 1 is best. The engine picks the highest-ranked strategy whose preconditions the target actually satisfies — it never defaults to purchasing.

strategies.label: Manufacturer-sponsored evaluation unit — $0 vehicle + $0 freight
strategies.ask: One evaluation unit provided at no cost, freight included, to establish the product at our location ahead of an initial inventory order.
what_we_offer: Committed first inventory order on successful evaluation
Local market entry in an under-served territory
Photos, video and field feedback from real-world evaluation
Display presence and service capability in-market
strategies.typical_objection: We don't place free units with unestablished dealers.
strategies.counter: Offer the credited structure (rank 6) as the fallback in the same conversation, so a 'no' converts rather than ends.

strategies.label: Distributor-sponsored demo unit
strategies.ask: A distributor-placed demo unit at no cost to establish a local sales channel in our territory.
what_we_offer: A new downstream retail outlet for the distributor's line
Territory coverage the distributor currently lacks
Initial stocking order once the demo proves out
strategies.typical_objection: Demo units are reserved for stocking dealers.
strategies.counter: Ask what stocking threshold unlocks a demo, then negotiate the threshold or the credit.

strategies.label: Dealer demo transfer — take an existing dealer's aging demo
strategies.ask: Transfer of an existing demo/floor unit that has aged out of the current selling season.
what_we_offer: Frees their floor space and floor-plan interest
strategies.counter: Position against their carrying cost: aged demo units cost them interest and depreciation every month.

strategies.label: $0 unit, buyer pays freight
strategies.approval_reason: Commits out-of-pocket freight cost — exceeds the $0 landed-cost objective.
strategies.ask: $0 vehicle with freight arranged and paid by us.
negotiate_next: Ask for freight at their negotiated carrier rate rather than retail LTL
Ask whether we can pick up to eliminate freight entirely

strategies.label: Demo cost 100% credited against first inventory order
strategies.approval_reason: Requires paying up front and committing to a first order; net-zero only if the order happens.
strategies.ask: Demo unit at dealer cost with 100% of that cost credited against our first 5-10 unit inventory order.
must_capture: Order size that triggers the credit
What happens if the first order is smaller than projected
strategies.note: Most achievable genuinely-net-zero structure. Push for this the moment a free unit is declined.

strategies.label: Previous-model-year unit at or near cost
strategies.ask: Non-current model-year unit at dealer cost or below, ideally with credit toward the first order.

strategies.label: Excess / overstock inventory
strategies.ask: Overstock unit at liquidation pricing with freight included.

strategies.label: Customer-cancelled order
strategies.ask: Any cancelled/refused order sitting unsold — taken off their hands at cost.

strategies.label: Cosmetic-blemish / freight-damaged unit
strategies.ask: Cosmetically blemished or freight-damaged unit that is mechanically sound — cosmetics are acceptable for an evaluation unit.
strategies.note: Strong angle: blemished units are hard for them to retail but perfectly serviceable as a demo, so the discount can be extreme.

strategies.label: Deeply discounted dealer sample
strategies.ask: Single sample unit at sample pricing to validate quality before a container/stocking order.
strategies.note: Common structure with overseas manufacturers: sample price is often credited on the first container order — always ask for that credit in writing.

strategies.label: Retail purchase — final fallback only
strategies.approval_reason: Full out-of-pocket cost. Contradicts the campaign objective; only valid once all other channels are documented as exhausted.
strategies.blocked_until: All strategies ranked 1-11 have been attempted or ruled out with recorded evidence for this target.
strategies.note: The engine will not select this automatically. It must be chosen by a human.

concession_ladder._comment: Stage 9. When $0 landed is refused, walk DOWN this ladder, extracting the highest item still available. Never volunteer a lower rung before the higher one is explicitly refused.

items.label: 100% of unit cost credited to first order

rules: Never claim a competing offer that does not exist.
Any market price cited must carry a source URL and retrieval date.
Never accept a paid offer automatically — every cost commitment goes to the human.
Trade only things actually within the profile's constraints (e.g. a first-order commitment requires constraints.willing_to_commit_first_order = true).
If the counterparty asks for payment before any verification, stop and flag the target.
